values.title: Never rebuild
values.text: Tack is a remote cache and executor for Bazel, Gradle, Nx and Turborepo. Point your build at it with one command, and every laptop and CI runner shares the same finished work.

values.title: Hashes in, finished work out
values.intro: Tack sits between the build tool you already use and every machine that runs it. No new build language and nothing to rewrite.
values.coreText: Looks up every task in 14 regional cache nodes and hands back the outputs if any machine has run it before.

values.title: Install Tack and run your first cached build
values.text: The CLI is a single 11 MB binary for macOS, Linux and Windows. It detects your build tool and writes the remote cache settings for you.
values.output:
✓ Installed tack 3.4.0
✓ Found Turborepo 2.5 in turbo.json
Run tack login to connect this repo.

values.title: A build cache you can see inside
values.text: The dashboard lists every task in a run, its cache key and the commit that first produced it. When a task misses, Tack names the input that changed.

image.alt: The Tack dashboard showing one CI run: 214 tasks, 212 restored from cache and two misses with the changed file named

values.title: Fast by default, strict where it counts
values.intro: Four parts of Tack that teams switch on in the first week and never think about again.

items.title: Forks cannot poison main
items.text: Pull requests read from the cache, but only protected branches write to it. One switch per workspace.

items.title: Keys that know the platform
items.text: The OS, CPU and toolchain version are part of every cache key, so a Mac never restores a Linux binary.

items.title: A hit rate you can watch
items.text: Every workspace shows its hit rate by branch and by task, and marks the commit where it started to fall.

items.title: Ask why a task missed
items.text: One command names the file, flag or environment variable that changed the key, and who changed it.

values.title: Every run, one keystroke away
values.intro: Press ⌘K anywhere in the Tack dashboard to jump to a run, a task or the commit that broke your hit rate.

values.title: Speaks the protocol your build already uses
values.intro: Tack implements the Bazel Remote Execution API, the Gradle HTTP build cache and the Nx and Turborepo cache APIs. There is no plugin to install or keep up to date.

values.title: Worker minutes that never expire
values.intro: Remote execution is optional and paid for with credits. One credit runs one vCPU for one minute on a Tack worker.

values.title: Pricing, the short version
values.intro: What engineering managers ask before they put a card in.

items.question: Is there a free plan?
items.detail: One developer or any public repository, with 10 GB of cache.

items.question: Do you charge per cache read?
items.detail: Reads and writes are unlimited. You pay for team size only.

items.question: Do CI runners count as seats?
items.detail: Only people who push commits in a month are counted.

items.question: Can we pay monthly?
items.detail: Month to month costs 20% more than the yearly price.

items.question: Do unused credits expire?
items.detail: Credits stay in the workspace until a cache miss spends them.

items.question: Windows remote workers?
items.detail: Private beta today, planned for everyone in 3.6.

releases.title: Faster cold restores and tack why
releases.text: Cache entries are now compressed with Zstandard dictionaries trained on your own artifacts, which makes cold restores 38% faster on a typical JavaScript monorepo. And when a task misses, tack why names the exact input that changed.

changes.text: tack why names the file, flag or variable that changed a cache key
Zstandard dictionary compression, on by default
Cold restores are 38% faster on repositories over 1 GB
tack login opens the browser correctly under WSL 2
Gradle configuration cache no longer misses after a JDK patch update
Uploads resume after a dropped connection instead of starting over

releases.title: Read-only tokens for forks
releases.text: Pull requests from forks can read from the cache without being able to write to it. Open source projects get warm builds for outside contributors with no risk to main.

changes.text: Read-only tokens, issued per pull request and revoked on merge
Cache regions in São Paulo and Mumbai, 14 in total
Dashboard run pages load in under 300 ms
Nx project graph hashes are stable across Windows and Linux

releases.title: Remote execution for Gradle tests
releases.text: Gradle test tasks can now run on Tack workers, split across up to 64 machines using timings from earlier runs.

changes.text: Remote execution for Gradle test tasks
Test splitting by historical timing, up to 64 workers
Worker cold start is down from 9 s to 2.5 s
Turborepo cache signatures verify correctly after a key rotation

releases.title: Storage limits you control
releases.text: Set a storage limit per project and Tack evicts the least recently used entries first. A full cache no longer fails a build.

changes.text: Per-project storage limits with least recently used eviction
tack doctor checks proxy and certificate settings
Bazel action cache no longer returns stale entries after a toolchain change
